messages:
sara_support: heads-up — customer reporting intermittent streaming disconnects and truncated output. Server logs show repeated write errors right before disconnect: 
```
  runtime: write error: write tcp 10.0.1.5:443->10.0.2.9:45322: write: broken pipe\n  runtime: write queue full for conn id=0x7fae3c, queued_bytes=1048576\n```

sara_support: happened ~10% of sessions for them since yesterday's runtime rollout. customer is seeing partial SSE events (last chunk missing) then abrupt connection close.

mike_sre: can you paste a minimal repro / request they used? which client and region? :mag_right:

sara_support: customer uses EventSource polyfill in node (node-fetch + eventsource), region us-east-1, model redwood/fast-chat-v1. payloads are large (8k–12k chars), they don't chunk messages on client. quick repro curl they shared:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/fast-chat-v1","input":"'$(python -c 'print("x"*10000)')'"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v2/streams
```

tom_runtime: I see the same pattern in our traces — before the EPIPE we emit a "write_queue_full" and then runtime aborts the connection to protect worker memory. looks like per-connection buffer cap is 1MB. slow consumer + big first payload fills queue quickly.

sara_support: customer tried switching to smaller chunking on their side and it improved stability (chunk_size=512). they also repro'd by artificially slowing reads (sleep 3s between reads).

mike_sre: can you repro in staging with slow clients? if we can reproduce we should decide whether to increase buffer or fail earlier with a clear error.

tom_runtime: reproduced locally: run 50 concurrent EventSource clients that read very slowly and send 10KB initial payloads. after ~30s some connections hit the queue cap and runtime closes with EPIPE. attaching snippet (pseudo):
```
# spawn 50 slow clients reading 1 chunk every 3s -> causes backpressure
for i in 1..50; do node slow_eventsource_test.js & done
```

tom_runtime: root cause = backpressure from slow consumers + large initial payloads. runtime currently uses a hard per-conn cap to avoid OOM across worker processes. when cap is reached we abort rather than giving a graceful 429/try-later.

sara_support: customer wants clear guidance on mitigation and whether we can avoid abrupt closes. they reported impact on their UX.

mike_sre: suggested short-term mitigations: 1) ask customer to enable client-side chunking / smaller initial prompt, 2) set TCP keepalive / shorter read timeouts on client, 3) we can add documentation + a clear 429-like streaming error instead of abrupt close.

tom_runtime: long-term: propose change to runtime: emit a slow_consumer metric, surface a descriptive error event ("slow_consumer_close") in SSE before closing, and explore adaptive per-conn buffering that trades off fairness. filing ENG-3421 to track design/rollback.

mike_sre: also propose adding a staging test that simulates slow readers to catch regressions on future rollouts. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: rollout note — runtime v2.14 deployment on 2025-03-01 was partially rolled back for us-east-1 after support reports.

sara_support: I'll send the customer the short-term mitigation steps (chunking + smaller first chunk) and let them know we have an internal ticket. will follow up here with their acceptance test results. :pray:

mike_sre: thanks — please include client repro script and the customer's exact headers if they can share. we'll prioritize ENG-3421 after triage.
